findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. A first-time reader can explain the product after this one paragraph.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The second section is an error message, and it sits right under the pitch. The pitch promises a commit traced to the models, cost and verdict, but this section shows none of them, so the first evidence a newcomer meets is missing. It should be fixed or removed.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: The page is about two projects at once: Athena, the product being pitched, and firstmate, the project being explained. The lede says how they relate, but almost all of the page body is about firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to work out that the page is itself the demonstration.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work" and "This page is that study of firstmate."

findings.text: This link in the header speaks to the site owner, not to a first-time visitor. A newcomer won't know what the proposals are or whose decision is meant.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: what to install first, the clone command, the setup script and a first command to try. The header also links straight to this section, so a newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The firstmate explanation is careful. It defines terms before using them, walks through one task from start to finish, and says plainly where something has no limit. A reader who wants that level of detail is well served.
findings.source: Start here / "Words used first" and the Glossary

findings.text: Several glossary entries define nothing: they only say the source does not define the term. That is honest, but it leaves gaps a newcomer cannot fill from this page.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a captain call." / "The firstmate source does not define a heartbeat." / "The firstmate source does not define a wake."

findings.text: This closing note is about how the page is built, which means nothing to a newcomer. It adds noise without helping them understand the page or decide what to do.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
